purpose: Compare source-session provenance and private-claim architectures without transferring qualification across protocol families or modes.
comparison_rules: Do not compare latency unless source bytes, claim/predicate, privacy objective, hardware and adversary model match.
A cryptographic proof is not source truth, account ownership, issuer authority, currentness, consent or action authority.
An attestor/notary/TEE is an explicit trust role even when its output is signed or later zero-knowledge verified.
A post-quantum signature on one layer does not promote the complete pipeline to post-quantum security.

profiles.witness_role: relying verifier participates online in TLS
privacy_notes: verifier learns encrypted traffic during session, not application plaintext
server identity privacy is a protocol-specific property
profiles.claim_limit: No offline public portability unless additional signed witness/receipt is introduced.

profiles.witness_role: delegated notary participates online and signs Session Header
privacy_notes: notary is designed not to learn plaintext or server identity
session timing, lengths, round counts and cipher metadata may leak
trust_assumptions: exact Session Header and commitment profile
profiles.claim_limit: Portable attestation is not trustless; offline verifier inherits trust in delegated witness.

profiles.witness_role: verifier proxies encrypted packets and observes server path
profiles.claim_limit: Must not inherit MPC-TLS identity privacy or direct connection assumptions.

profiles.witness_role: measured TEE runs verifier during MPC-TLS while prover retains TLS decryption/plaintext
profiles.portability: attested verifier receipt under TEE vendor/image/TCB trust profile
privacy_notes: enclave sees protocol/ciphertext material but must not receive TLS write/decryption keys or application plaintext
privacy remains cryptographic and prover-side only if the no-plaintext dataflow invariant is demonstrated
trust_assumptions: exact TEE vendor attestation root and current TCB
correct TLSNotary verifier code and protocol
profiles.claim_limit: Improves delegated verifier integrity under TEE assumptions without automatically moving plaintext into the enclave; any key/plaintext ingress changes the profile to TEE plaintext processor.

privacy_profiles.tradeoff: Not selective privacy. Entire response reaches verifier.

privacy_profiles.description: Only chosen HTTP objects/ranges are revealed; other response fields remain redacted.
privacy_profiles.tradeoff: Requires the relevant commitment/opening and plaintext proof path.

privacy_profiles.description: At least one sensitive byte/field remains hidden in the direction.
privacy_profiles.tradeoff: Full-reveal fast path does not apply; direction uses ZK path.

profiles.witness_role: prover and verifier jointly participate with server
privacy_notes: context integrity binds disclosed substring to expected location/context
profiles.claim_limit: Original DECO research construction targets TLS 1.2; do not infer TLS1.3 support from DIDO+.

published_baseline.qualification: Original research paper and implementation are a baseline; not matched here to TLSNotary Beta.1 or current RISC Zero workload.

profiles.claim_limit: TLS1.3 capability applies only to exact DIDO+ construction and implementation; no inheritance to other TLS provenance systems.

published_baseline.qualification: Published in IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing, November 2025; no directly comparable measurements included in this matrix.

profiles.witness_role: proxy mode commonly used; MPC mode fallback where proxy path is restricted
privacy_notes: proxy mode reveals server identity to verifier
MPC mode has substantial communication overhead
profiles.claim_limit: Do not call hybrid mode a single trust model; profile actual session mode and exact release.

profiles.witness_role: TEE_K holds TLS keys/connection; TEE_T computes authentication tags without key access
privacy_notes: split service roles reduce single-service view under exact implementation
TLS1.2 CBC compatibility path has a different trust boundary
trust_assumptions: AMD SEV / cloud Confidential VM attestation chain where used
exact image measurements and TCB version
profiles.claim_limit: Valid hardware quote is insufficient without matching exact image/configuration and dataflow roles.

published_baseline.qualification: Published code and Trust Package are useful evidence, not a substitute for independently verifying a live deployment's hardware quote, image measurement and configuration.

profiles.witness_role: attestation node witnesses TLS provenance and extracts/signs commitment
privacy_notes: private value and salt hidden by proof
application-scoped spend tag introduces controlled linkability
profiles.claim_limit: Fresh salt can create new commitment/spend tag for same account; Falcon signature authenticates root signer but not correct append-only state transition.
profiles.additional_replay_risk: A fresh salt can generate a different commitment and spend tag for the same Web2 account. Application uniqueness therefore requires a separately qualified domain-scoped subject binding; account uniqueness does not establish person uniqueness.

published_baseline.samples: 10 STARK repetitions; 10 aggregator repetitions; 5 gas repetitions
published_baseline.qualification: Paper-reported research data; threshold-only benchmark is not an end-to-end source/predicate/authority cost; do not compare directly with TLSNotary Beta.1.

benchmark_manifest.fixture: synthetic HTTPS financial API; fixed request/response bytes; local deterministic server; test certificate chain frozen; no real credentials or personal data
benchmark_manifest.claim: currency == ZAR AND available_minor_units >= required_minimum_minor_units AND as_of is within the declared freshness window
fairness_rules: Same exact request and response bytes wherever protocol allows.
Do not compare proxy with MPC/TEE/notary as equal security modes.
Include source/session witness and credential checks, not just local proof time.
Report preprocessing separately from online latency.
Report all failures and rejected controls; rejecting all inputs is not a valid positive-control pass.
Uniqueness subject must be frozen as account, credential, entitlement, application or person; different subject claims are not interchangeable.
Do not compare full-response-reveal runtime with selective-disclosure runtime without reporting that the verifier receives the whole response in the former.
Pin exact TLSNotary release/tag/full source commit, crate graph, feature flags, Rust toolchain and target; prerelease Beta.1 remains an integration candidate, not a certified verifier.
Treat attested MPC-TLS verifier with prover-side plaintext and TEE plaintext processor as different privacy/trust profiles.

prospective_targets.latency_superiority: Only claim after matched end-to-end benchmark under equal security, privacy, authority and hardware budgets; proposed aim is >=20% lower p95 time-to-qualified-private-decision without increasing leakage or false accepts.

nonclaims: No system in this matrix is certified or promoted by inclusion.
Reported performance from separate papers/vendor posts is not a matched leaderboard.
Transport authenticity does not establish provider truth or account ownership.
Proof validity does not establish currentness, policy authority, consent or external effect.
Salted-commitment-derived spend tags do not guarantee uniqueness across fresh attestations for the same account.
Application/account-scoped uniqueness does not prove uniqueness of a legal or natural person.

TLSNotary full-reveal fast path is not selective disclosure: entire traffic direction is disclosed; only the key-derivation ZK proof remains while the ciphertext-to-plaintext proof for that direction is skipped.
A TEE verifier can strengthen delegated witness integrity without sacrificing prover-side plaintext confidentiality only if no TLS decryption material or application plaintext enters the enclave.
